fluff.overview: The Regent is a 90-ton assault OmniMech introduced in 3145 as the flagship product of Clan Sea Fox's ilKhanate Project Reynard. Born from a unique three-way partnership between Coventry Metal Works, Technicron Manufacturing, and the ilKhanate, the Regent fills the role previously occupied by the Hauptmann OmniMech, which had been shelved following the Jihad and Devlin Stone's military reduction programs. Coventry Metal Works sought to resurrect the Hauptmann concept using Clan-grade technology, but found domestic ClanTech manufacturers overstretched. Merchant Bilius of Clan Sea Fox brokered a novel arrangement through the Chatterweb: CMW and Technicron would each build the base chassis at their respective factories on Coventry and Savannah, while ilKhanate facilities would arm the completed frames with Clan OmniPods for sale to all buyers. The resulting design incorporates elements of both the Hauptmann and the Awesome, earning it the nickname "Awesomemann" among MechWarriors who pilot it.
fluff.capabilities:
The Regent serves as a philosophy of rugged simplicity over cutting-edge technology. Built on a Reynard Standard Type chassis powered by a GM 270 standard fusion engine, the design deliberately eschews weight-saving measures like extralight engines or endo steel construction. This conservative approach yields exceptional battlefield survivability, as the loss of a side torso will not destroy the 'Mech. Thick Durallex Special Heavy armor provides protection comparable to the heaviest assault designs, while the standard engine and structure ensure straightforward maintenance and repair across diverse logistical environments.

With 43 tons of available pod space, the Regent supports a wide range of alternate configurations from dedicated fire support platforms to devastating short-range brawlers. This generous payload allowance, combined with Clan OmniPod technology, gives commanders extraordinary flexibility to tailor the 'Mech to specific mission requirements. The design's primary limitations are its lack of jump capability and relatively modest speed of 54 km/h, making it dependent on favorable terrain and good tactical positioning to bring its considerable firepower to bear. Heat management varies significantly between configurations, requiring pilots to familiarize themselves thoroughly with the thermal characteristics of their chosen loadout.
fluff.history:
The Regent's origins trace to the collapse of Hauptmann production following the Word of Blake Jihad, when Devlin Stone's military reduction programs shuttered numerous 'Mech production lines across the Inner Sphere. Coventry Metal Works, long associated with the Hauptmann, found itself without a signature assault OmniMech as the Dark Age's fragile peace began to deteriorate. When CMW attempted to revive the design with Clan-grade double heat sink technology, they discovered that domestic ClanTech manufacturers in the Lyran Commonwealth were already overstretched by existing supply contracts and unable to accommodate the project.

Clan Sea Fox's ilKhanate, ever alert for commercial opportunities, identified this gap through the Chatterweb. Merchant Bilius orchestrated one of the era's most innovative manufacturing arrangements, a three-way partnership designated Project Reynard. Legal negotiations, mediated by the ilKhanate itself, produced a deal where Coventry Metal Works and Free Worlds League-based Technicron Manufacturing would each build the base chassis for exclusive Sea Fox purchase. The ilKhanate would then arm the completed OmniMechs with Clan OmniPods for sale to all buyers, adding another accomplishment to the ilKhanate's growing portfolio of cross-border commercial ventures.

Clan Sea Fox has spread the Regent across multiple markets, selling to both the Lyran Commonwealth and the Free Worlds League. The 'Mech saw early combat during a clash between the Third Marik Protectors and elements of the Magistracy Cavaliers on Rohinjan in 3148, where a Force Commander's Regent proved its worth by dismantling a pirate Atlas and driving off its lance-mates. The design has also attracted interest from displaced Lyran nobles building private forces along the Periphery border, demonstrating the broad appeal of a powerful yet maintainable assault OmniMech.

Not all within Clan Sea Fox have welcomed Project Reynard's success. The Spina and Tiburon Khanates have expressed resentment at what they view as overreach by the ilKhanate's merchants, reflecting ongoing tensions within the Clan over commercial strategy and the distribution of manufacturing profits. Yet, the Regent's commercial performance and battlefield effectiveness have largely vindicated the project, establishing it as a model for future Clan Sea Fox industrial partnerships with Inner Sphere manufacturers.
fluff.deployment: The C configuration earns its "Fafnirmann" nickname through its dedication to overwhelming ballistic firepower, mirroring the philosophy of Defiance Industries' iconic Fafnir assault 'Mech. A Hyper-Assault Gauss 40 delivers devastating salvos at range, supported by four tons of ammunition for sustained engagements, while an Improved Heavy Gauss Rifle with three tons of ammunition provides a brutal secondary weapon capable of penetrating even the thickest armor. This configuration specializes in destroying targets through sheer volume and power of ballistic fire. However, it lacks any energy weapons whatsoever, making it entirely dependent on its ammunition supply for continued combat effectiveness, a significant vulnerability in extended operations far from resupply.
